# The canvas worker cannot load engine renderers in a workspace production build

## Context

devindex's first own Pages deploy (neomjs/devindex#27) is the first consumer-workspace production build that runs a canvas renderer from the engine. On `https://neomjs.github.io/devindex/`, the canvas worker logs:

```
Canvas Worker: Failed to load module src/canvas/Header Error: Cannot find module './src/canvas/Header.mjs'
Renderer Remote Stub not found: Neo.canvas.Header
Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'initGraph')
```

The app header's `Neo.app.header.Canvas` never gets its renderer.

## The Problem

`Neo.worker.Canvas#loadModule` resolves every renderer from one root, `import(\`../../${path}.mjs\`)` (`src/worker/Canvas.mjs`). Inside the engine repository, `../../` from `src/worker` is the repository root, so both engine renderers (`src/canvas/Header.mjs`) and app renderers (`apps/*/canvas/*.mjs`) resolve.

In a consumer workspace, `workerContextRebasePlugin` (`buildScripts/webpack/workerContextRebasePlugin.mjs`, #17882) rebases every non-package-local worker context root to the workspace. The canvas root `../..` is not package-local (`isPackageLocal()` accepts only `../data…`), so it becomes the workspace root. The engine's `src/canvas/*` lives under `node_modules/neo.mjs/`, so a `src/…` renderer path has no match. The rebase is right for `apps/…` renderers and wrong for the engine's own.

Measured: in the deployed `canvasworker.js` (neo 13.1.0's inline predecessor of the same rebase), the lazy context contains no engine renderer. `dev`'s `loadModule` and the plugin have the same shape.

Every engine renderer that a class names by an `src/canvas/…` `rendererImportPath` is affected in any workspace production build: `app.header.Canvas` (`src/canvas/Header.mjs`) and `component.Sparkline` (`src/canvas/Sparkline.mjs`).

## The Architectural Reality

- `SharedCanvas#rendererImportPath` passes engine paths (`src/canvas/Header.mjs`) and app paths through the same `loadModule`.
- The Data Worker hit the same split in #17882 and got explicit roots: package-local `../data` stays in the package, app space is rebased.
- `Canvas#onRegisterNeoConfig`'s `useCanvasWorkerStartingPoint` import has the same single root. It is app-space only (`apps/<app>/canvas.mjs`), so its rebase is correct.

## The Fix

Give `loadModule` two explicit roots, the way the Data Worker's imports were split. A path under `src/` imports from a package-local root (`../${rest}`, where `src/worker/../` is the package's `src/`). Any other path keeps the rebased app-space root. The plugin then needs no canvas exception: `../canvas…`-style roots are not rebased, which `isPackageLocal` has to learn, or the root is written so it already reads as package-local.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] In a consumer-workspace production build, `loadModule({path: 'src/canvas/Header.mjs'})` succeeds, and so does an app-space renderer (`apps/<app>/canvas/<X>.mjs`).
- [ ] Inside the engine repository (`insideNeo`), both still load.
- [ ] A build-level witness asserts both context maps, the way #17882's arms assert the Data Worker's roots.

## Out of Scope

- neomjs/devindex#34 (the Pages site's empty grid). The rehearsal build carried this same failure and still painted, so this defect is not what empties that grid.
